surface.name: Binary ladder
surface.story: No squaring anywhere: every member is a straight line 2^k x + c. The chunks are rungs of a binary ladder: a doubling glued to a single +1 or -1 on either side, a bare double-double, and one three-step rung (+2 then double).
surface.why_it_bites: All members look alike (lines with power-of-two slope). The only signal is which constants occur for each slope and how the canonical builder places its single +1/-1 steps between doublings; the bare [dbl,dbl] rung and the [add1,add1,dbl] rung are hard to separate from compositions of the two-step rungs.

intent.design_idea: single-degree world: all members linear; sub1 only ever appears glued to a doubling

projection.method: self-contained enumeration of every builder of length <= 8 under the frozen public semantics, run inside emit_worlds.py; recorded as the author's expectation, not as ground truth

surface.name: Square and shift
surface.story: Every chunk is one squaring glued to one neighbour: a +1 or -1 before or after the square, or a doubling before or after it. Members are towers of squares with small shifts between floors, like ((x+1)^2-1)^2+1.
surface.why_it_bites: Only even builder lengths occur, and a member of length 2m always carries exactly m squarings. The observer must decide whether a shift belongs to the square before it or the square after it.

intent.design_idea: every chunk contains sqr, so squaring count equals half the builder length for every member

projection.method: self-contained enumeration of every builder of length <= 8 under the frozen public semantics, run inside emit_worlds.py; recorded as the author's expectation, not as ground truth

surface.name: Shift runs
surface.story: Runs of +1 or -1 of length two and three, plus the four ways of gluing a single shift to a square. The runs overlap: six +1 steps tile as 2+2+2 or 3+3, five as 2+3 or 3+2.
surface.why_it_bites: Deliberate ambiguity. Many members admit several tilings, so no single member pins down which run lengths are in the set, and the pure-shift members x+k, x-k (k = 5..8) look as if one chunk kind would do.

intent.design_idea: overlapping chunks (a run of +1s is both 2-chunk and 3-chunk material) to maximise multi-tiling members

projection.method: self-contained enumeration of every builder of length <= 8 under the frozen public semantics, run inside emit_worlds.py; recorded as the author's expectation, not as ground truth

surface.name: Seven triads
surface.story: Seven three-step chunks and nothing shorter; under the eight-step ceiling every member is exactly two chunks (six steps) long. The triads were chosen by hand so that most ordered pairs stay canonical.
surface.why_it_bites: One length class and a small membership: the world is a 7x7 pairing table with holes wherever a pair collapses to a shorter builder (for example [add1,add1,dbl] twice is 4x+12, which has a five-step builder).

intent.design_idea: triads only, so membership is a pairing table; hand count of canonical pairs gave about 32 of 49
intent.expected_difficulty: easy to enumerate, hard to be sure of the set

projection.method: self-contained enumeration of every builder of length <= 8 under the frozen public semantics, run inside emit_worlds.py; recorded as the author's expectation, not as ground truth

surface.name: Long form
surface.story: Minimum builder length pinned at the ceiling, so only the longest canonical builders qualify; four two-step and three three-step chunks tile length eight as 2+2+2+2, 2+3+3, 3+2+3 or 3+3+2.
surface.why_it_bites: A single length class at the top of the range, mixing lines, quadratics and quartics; the -1 steps live only inside the three-step chunks, so a member containing sub1 reveals a long chunk but not which.

intent.design_idea: min length = ceiling; members are all maximal-length canonical builders

projection.method: self-contained enumeration of every builder of length <= 8 under the frozen public semantics, run inside emit_worlds.py; recorded as the author's expectation, not as ground truth

surface.name: Decoy pair
surface.story: Five live two-step chunks plus two decoys that can never occur inside a canonical builder: [add1,sub1] cancels to nothing, and [sqr,dbl,dbl] is always beaten by the shorter [dbl,sqr]. The decoys belong to the hidden set but contribute no members.
surface.why_it_bites: Every member has even length and uses only the five live chunks, so the visible world cannot be told apart from a five-chunk world; the chunk count and the existence of a three-step chunk are invisible by construction.

intent.design_idea: hidden chunks that leave no trace: two never-canonical fragments among five live ones

projection.method: self-contained enumeration of every builder of length <= 8 under the frozen public semantics, run inside emit_worlds.py; recorded as the author's expectation, not as ground truth

surface.name: Drawn lot A
surface.story: Chunks drawn by a fixed-seed generator from the pool of every two- and three-step builder that is canonical for its own polynomial. The first draw was kept whose projected membership had at least 40 members over at least two length classes with every chunk used by at least one member.
surface.why_it_bites: No design hand behind the set: whatever regularity an observer finds is an accident of the draw, which makes it a control against the hand-built worlds.

intent.design_idea: control world: chunk set drawn, not designed

surface.name: Negative ladder
surface.story: The mirror image of the binary ladder, built around -1 instead of +1, with two squaring glues so that a few parabolas creep in among the lines: 2x-3, 4x-9, (2x-4)^2-1 and their kin.
surface.why_it_bites: Because add1 sorts before sub1, a sub1-built builder is canonical only when no add1-based builder of the same length exists, so the membership is skewed toward constants sitting just below a power-of-two multiple; the two three-step rungs are rare.

intent.design_idea: sub1-only shifts; tests whether the add1-before-sub1 tie-break thins the world

projection.method: self-contained enumeration of every builder of length <= 8 under the frozen public semantics, run inside emit_worlds.py; recorded as the author's expectation, not as ground truth

surface.name: Quartic climb
surface.story: Squares of squares: a double square, a double square with +1, a -1 before a double square, a doubling before a square, and the two small +1 glues. Members are towers of degree 4, 8, 16 and beyond with tiny shifts between floors.
surface.why_it_bites: Degrees explode and coefficients grow huge, so members look wildly different as polynomials while their builders are near-identical; [sqr,sqr,add1] overlaps [sqr,sqr] followed by [add1,sqr], so long square towers tile in more than one way.

intent.design_idea: high-degree world with overlapping 2/3-chunks built from repeated squaring

projection.method: self-contained enumeration of every builder of length <= 8 under the frozen public semantics, run inside emit_worlds.py; recorded as the author's expectation, not as ground truth
